## 4. SKILL.md frontmatter catalog (name + description)

1. **grill-with-docs** — A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
2. **tdd** — Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
3. **diagnosing-bugs** — Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
4. **zoom-out** — Tell the agent to zoom out and give broader context or a higher-level perspective. Use when you're unfamiliar with a section of code or need to understand how it fits into the bigger picture. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`; frozen skill)*
5. **to-prd** — Turn the current conversation into a PRD and publish it to the project issue tracker — no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
6. **to-issues** — Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable issues on the project issue tracker using tracer-bullet vertical slices. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
7. **improve-codebase-architecture** — Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
8. **triage** — Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles — categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
9. **prototype** — Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

# Docs structure & conventions report — for adding a Matt Pocock collection page

## 1. Overall `docs/` tree structure

The site is MkDocs Material with a bilingual (`i18n` suffix) setup. Every published page has a `*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md` pair. Top-level organization:

```
docs/
  index.md                     Home
  getting-started.md
  conventions.md
  changelog.md
  _snippets/                   EN-only include fragments (NOT rendered as pages)
    install.md
    external-install.md        <- status-enum single source of truth
    domain-hub-template.md     <- the domain hub _template (EN-only)
  workflows/                   How-to guides
    adding-vendor-skills.md
    adding-catalog-entries.md  <- catalog recipe
    creating-local-skills.md
    project-memory.md
  skills/                      One page per shipped skill (local + vendored) + index.md
    index.md, <skill>.md ...
  catalog/                     Vendoring decision log + external awareness
    index.md
    skill-collections.md       <- the upstream-collections index
    domains/                   Per-domain hub pages + index.md
      index.md, finance.md, quant-research.md, ai-ml-research.md,
      web-fullstack.md, knowledge-work.md, agent-harness.md
    mcp/                        MCP wiki (index.md + one page per MCP)
      index.md, financialdatasets-ai.md
  reference/                   Landscape / convention pages (things we consume, not ship)
    warp-oz-skills.md, deep-research-landscape.md, sdd-and-harnesses.md,
    llm-wiki-pattern.md, npx-skills-metadata.md, tag-schema.md, ... (16 pages)
```

`docs/catalog/` has three subareas per `CLAUDE.md`: `domains/` (per-domain hubs), `skill-collections.md` (single upstream-collections index), and `mcp/` (MCP wiki). It is explicitly "the vendoring decision log + external-awareness registry," distinct from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our own conventions).

## 3. `docs/catalog/domains/` hubs + the template

**Hub pages present:** `finance.md`, `quant-research.md`, `ai-ml-research.md`, `web-fullstack.md`, `knowledge-work.md`, `agent-harness.md` (each + `.zh-TW.md`), plus `index.md`.

**Template** (`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`, EN-only) structure:
- `# {{Domain name}}` + one-line elevator pitch.
- `## Skills in this repo` → `### Local` (table `Skill | One-line | Notes`) and `### Vendored` (table `Skill | Upstream | Series`).
- `## External skills (manual install)` → `--8<-- "_snippets/external-install.md"` include, then table `Skill / Plugin | Upstream | Status | Why this status | Install hint`.
- `## MCP servers` → table `Name | Upstream | Status | Auth | Records`.

- `## See also` → reference-landscape + adjacent-hub links.
- Header comment instructs: copy to `docs/catalog/domains/<slug>.md`, add to `mkdocs.yml` nav under `Catalog → Domains`, and keep `_none yet_` placeholders rather than padding.

**How skills are referenced in a hub:** by backticked skill name, linked either to its `docs/skills/<name>.md` page (for shipped skills) or to the upstream repo (for external ones). The Vendored table cites the `Series` column (e.g. `engineering-fundamentals`, `fullstack-nextjs`).

So there's no perfectly-matching populated hub; the engineering-fundamentals series is vendored but under-represented in the domains layer.

## 4. Bilingual convention — confirmed

`CLAUDE.md` line 238-239: *"Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`). Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention."*

Confirmed by the file listing — every `docs/catalog/` page is paired:
- `catalog/index.md` + `catalog/index.zh-TW.md`
- `catalog/skill-collections.md` + `catalog/skill-collections.zh-TW.md`
- `catalog/domains/{index,finance,quant-research,ai-ml-research,web-fullstack,knowledge-work,agent-harness}.md` + each `.zh-TW.md`
- `catalog/mcp/{index,financialdatasets-ai}.md` + each `.zh-TW.md`

EN-only exceptions (no zh-TW twin): `_snippets/install.md`, `_snippets/external-install.md`, `_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`.

**How the zh-TW files are structured:** they are **full standalone translations**, not stubs and not references back to EN. `skill-collections.zh-TW.md` (103 lines vs the EN's 95) mirrors the EN section-for-section and row-for-row, translating prose and table headers while leaving code, repo names, CLI flags, filenames, and the backticked `status` enum untranslated. It opens with an extra admonition block absent from EN — the zh-TW terminology rule:

```
!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"
    技術名詞首次出現以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，例：依賴注入
    (dependency injection)。**不自創翻譯**——若無公認譯名直接保留英文
    （如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`）。代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。
```

Both files pull the **same** shared `--8<-- "_snippets/external-install.md"` include (the snippet is EN-only, so the enum table renders in English on both). The i18n plugin uses `fallback_to_default: true`, so a missing translation won't break the build, but the project rule is both languages land in the same PR.

## 5. `mkdocs.yml` nav wiring

Path: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/mkdocs.yml`. Key mechanics:
- `plugins.i18n` with `docs_structure: suffix`, `fallback_to_default: true`, locales `en` (default) + `zh-TW`. Only the EN `*.md` paths appear in `nav:`; zh-TW is auto-derived from the suffix.
- `plugins.llmstxt.sections.Catalog` globs `catalog/*.md`, `catalog/domains/*.md`, `catalog/mcp/*.md` — a new `catalog/*.md` page is auto-picked-up by the llms.txt output.
- `pymdownx.snippets.base_path` includes `.`, `docs`, `docs/_snippets` (that's why `--8<-- "_snippets/external-install.md"` resolves).

**The `Catalog` nav block (lines 142-155):**

```yaml
  - Catalog:
      - Overview: catalog/index.md
      - Domains:
          - Overview: catalog/domains/index.md
          - Finance: catalog/domains/finance.md
          - Quant Research: catalog/domains/quant-research.md
          - AI/ML Research: catalog/domains/ai-ml-research.md
          - Web & Fullstack: catalog/domains/web-fullstack.md
          - Knowledge Work: catalog/domains/knowledge-work.md
          - Agent Harness: catalog/domains/agent-harness.md
      - External skills: catalog/skill-collections.md
      - MCP wiki:
          - Overview: catalog/mcp/index.md
          - Financial Datasets: catalog/mcp/financialdatasets-ai.md
```

**Where a new collection/series page would register:** there is **no existing "Collections" nav group** — `skill-collections.md` sits as a single leaf `External skills:` under `Catalog`. Grouping patterns that already exist you could mirror:
- Under `Catalog`: the `Domains:` and `MCP wiki:` sub-groups each use an `Overview:` index page + sibling leaves. A new "Collections" or "Series deep-dives" sub-group would follow that shape.
- Under `Skills` → `Vendored` (lines 127-141): the `Fullstack Next.js:` **series** is a nested nav group listing each skill page. This is the established "series grouping" precedent in nav — but note it lists individual skill pages, not a single series-intro page.
- Under `Reference` (lines 156-171): flat leaves, where the single-author deep-dives (`Warp Oz skills`, `Deep Research landscape`) currently live.

`not_in_nav: /_snippets/` suppresses the snippet/template from nav. `validation.links.not_found: info` keeps `--strict` builds passing.

**Gap worth flagging:** the `engineering-fundamentals` (mattpocock) and `product-planning` series are vendored in `vendor.yaml` / `skills/vendor/` but have **no** individual `docs/skills/*.md` pages and **no** nav entries — only `fullstack-nextjs` is documented under `Skills → Vendored`. So a mattpocock page would be net-new documentation surface, and there's a decision to make about whether to also add the 9 individual skill pages the way `fullstack-nextjs` did.

## 6. Status-enum source of truth + catalog recipe

**`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`** is the status-enum single source of truth. It's an admonition block: *"Status enum (single source of truth across the catalog)"* with a 5-row table:

| Status | Meaning | Where it links |
|---|---|---|
| `vendored` | Already in `vendor.yaml`. | Link to `skills/vendor/<name>/` (or series). |
| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` — under consideration. | Link to the `TODO.md` anchor. |
| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor. | Inline reason required (1 sentence). |
| `evaluated` | Read but no decision. Effectively "tracked." | Inline 1-line note. |
| `wishlist` | Surfaced, not yet evaluated. | No link required; default for fresh discoveries. |

- writing-great-skills — reference for writing and editing skills: vocabulary and principles that make skills predictable. — productivity / user-invoked

- grilling — reusable interview loop that interviews the user until every branch of a decision tree is resolved (backing grill-me / grill-with-docs). — productivity / model-invoked

- How the author frames the collection: a compact, practical toolkit of small, composable agent skills the author actually uses day-to-day to do “real engineering” instead of shallow or performative work.

77	## Vendoring policy
78	
79	We vendor a skill when:
80	
81	1. The upstream has stable canonical authority (Vercel for Next.js, Supabase for Supabase, etc.).
82	2. The skill fills a gap not already covered by another vendored or local skill.
83	3. The license is compatible with the [agentskills.io specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).
84	
85	We **do not** vendor when:
86	
87	- The upstream is itself a marketplace / collection (we cherry-pick instead).
88	- Plugin-format collections (e.g., `anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins`) require `claude plugin install` rather than `npx skills add` — we record them here for manual install.
89	- The skill duplicates an already-vendored one from a more authoritative source.
90	- The skill is too narrow for general use (host-specific, BigQuery-specific, etc.).
91	
92	For the full workflow — including how to move an entry from `wishlist` →
93	`deferred` → `vendored` — see
94	[Adding catalog entries](../workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).

1	!!! info "Status enum (single source of truth across the catalog)"
2	
3	    Every external-skill or MCP entry below carries a `status:` value:
4	
5	    | Status | Meaning | Where it links |
6	    |---|---|---|
7	    | `vendored` | Already in [`vendor.yaml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/vendor.yaml). | Link to the `skills/vendor/<name>/` (or series) entry. |
8	    | `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — under consideration. | Link to the [`TODO.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/TODO.md) anchor. |
9	    | `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor. | Inline reason required (1 sentence). |
10	    | `evaluated` | Read but no decision recorded. Effectively "tracked." | Inline 1-line note describing what was learned. |
11	    | `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated. | No link required; default for fresh discoveries. |
12	
13	    Status changes are explicit edits — see the **Adding catalog
14	    entries** workflow doc (under `Workflows` in the nav) for the
15	    `wishlist → deferred → vendored` recipe.
16	
17	!!! tip "Manual install for non-vendored skills"
18	
19	    When a skill is not in `vendor.yaml`, you can still install it directly
20	    from upstream via the [`npx skills`](https://skills.sh) CLI:
21	
22	    ```bash
23	    # Whole-repo install (if SKILL.md sits at repo root or skills/)
24	    npx skills@latest add <owner>/<repo>
25	
26	    # Subpath install (when the skill is nested)
27	    npx skills@latest add <owner>/<repo>/<path-to-skill-dir>
28	
29	    # Cherry-pick by name
30	    npx skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> -s <skill-name>
31	
32	    # Force deep discovery (skill nested >1 level inside skills/)
33	    npx skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> --full-depth -s <skill-name>
34	    ```
35	
36	    For Anthropic-style **plugin marketplaces** (e.g.
37	    `anthropics/financial-services`,
38	    `anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins`), use the Claude Code plugin
39	    commands instead:
40	
41	    ```bash
42	    claude plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>
43	    claude plugin install <plugin-name>@<repo-name>
44	    ```
45	
46	    For MCP servers, see the per-entry "Auth & install" section in
47	    the MCP wiki — install commands vary by transport (HTTP / stdio /
48	    SSE) and host (Claude Code / Claude Desktop / Cursor / Managed
49	    Agents).
50
```

```text
1	# Adding catalog entries
2	
3	How to add or update entries in the [Catalog](../catalog/index.md) —
4	new external skills, new MCP servers, new domain hubs, or status
5	changes on existing entries.
6	
7	This workflow couples the catalog to `vendor.yaml` and `TODO.md` (the
8	existing sources of truth) without duplicating them. Catalog pages are
9	the *vendoring decision log*; the actual vendoring happens via existing
10	scripts.
11	
12	## When to write a catalog entry
13	
14	| You discovered… | Where it goes | Status to start with |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| An external skill you might want to vendor | [`skill-collections.md`](../catalog/skill-collections.md) + relevant [domain hub](../catalog/domains/index.md) | `wishlist` |
17	| An MCP server you want to remember | New file under [`catalog/mcp/`](../catalog/mcp/index.md) + relevant domain hub | `wishlist` |
18	| A whole new professional domain | New file under [`catalog/domains/`](../catalog/domains/index.md) (copy `_template.md`) | (hub itself, not entry) |
19	| A skill you looked at and rejected | Add to `skill-collections.md` with reason | `skipped` |
20	| A skill you looked at but didn't decide on | Add to `skill-collections.md` with 1-line note | `evaluated` |
21	
22	## Status enum
23	
24	--8<-- "_snippets/external-install.md"
25	
26	## Status change recipes
27	
28	### `wishlist` → `deferred`
29	
30	The entry has crossed into "we should evaluate this" territory.
31	
32	```bash
33	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P? --effort <S|M|L> \
34	  --title "<skill-name> skill" \
35	  --description "Evaluate <upstream URL> for <use case>. See catalog/<page>.md."
36	```
37	
38	Then edit the catalog entry: change `status: wishlist` → `status: deferred`,
39	link to the new TODO line.
40	
41	### `deferred` → `vendored`
42	
43	The entry has been evaluated and we want to vendor it.
44	
45	```bash
46	# Vendor the skill (writes to vendor.yaml + downloads files)
47	./scripts/add-vendor.sh <owner>/<repo>/<path-to-skill>
48	
49	# Or with a series subdir
50	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series <series-name> <owner>/<repo>/<path-to-skill>
51	
52	# If the entry had a TODO P? line, promote it
53	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" \
54	  --summary "Vendored from <upstream URL>"
55	```
56	
57	Then edit the catalog entry: change `status: deferred` → `status: vendored`,
58	update the link to point at `skills/vendor/<name>/` (or
59	`skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`).
60	
61	### `wishlist` / `evaluated` → `skipped`
62	
63	You read the upstream and decided not to vendor.
64	
65	Just edit the catalog entry: change status → `skipped`, add the reason
66	inline (one sentence). Examples:
67	
68	- "Skipped — duplicates `<other-skill>` from `<more-authoritative-source>`."
69	- "Skipped — Slack-specific; not portable."
70	- "Skipped — narrower than `<existing-local-skill>` and overlaps it."
71	
72	## Adding a new MCP entry
73	
74	1. Create `docs/catalog/mcp/<slug>.md` with the YAML frontmatter
75	   schema documented in [`mcp/index.md`](../catalog/mcp/index.md#per-entry-conventions).
76	2. Fill the 6-section body (TL;DR / capabilities / install / when /
77	   related / sources).
78	3. Translate to `docs/catalog/mcp/<slug>.zh-TW.md`.
79	4. Add to the `mkdocs.yml` nav under `Catalog → MCP wiki`.
80	5. Add a row to the entries table in
81	   [`mcp/index.md`](../catalog/mcp/index.md).
82	6. Cross-link from any relevant domain hub's MCP section.
83	
84	When the MCP wiki has 5+ entries, the index table will be regenerated
85	by a script (planned — see follow-up TODOs). Until then, edit the
86	table by hand.
87	
88	## Adding a new domain hub
89	
90	See the [How to add a new domain hub](../catalog/domains/index.md#how-to-add-a-new-domain-hub)
91	section in the Domains overview — the recipe lives next to the
92	template it references.
93	
94	## Bilingual obligation
95	
96	Every page in `docs/catalog/` (except the snippet and `_template.md`)
97	must have a `*.zh-TW.md` counterpart. The `mkdocs-i18n` plugin's
98	`fallback_to_default: true` means missing translations don't break the
99	build, but the project convention is that every published page has
100	both languages in the same PR.
101	
102	## Validation

1	# Agent Harness
2	
3	Spec-driven development (SDD) frameworks and agent harnesses — the layer
4	**above** agent skills that owns the requirements → spec → plan → tasks →
5	execute → verify loop, manages context windows, or runs sub-agents.
6	
7	This repo focuses on **skills** and intentionally does not ship a SDD
8	framework or harness, but skills are *consumed* by harnesses, so we track
9	the major options here for awareness.
10	
11	## Skills in this repo
12	
13	### Local
14	
15	| Skill | One-line | Notes |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| _none — out of scope_ | | We ship skills; harnesses ship the loop that orchestrates skills. Different layer. |
18	
19	### Vendored
20	
21	| Skill | Upstream | Series |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| _none — out of scope_ | | |
24	
25	## External skills (manual install)
26	
27	--8<-- "_snippets/external-install.md"
28	
29	| Skill / Plugin | Upstream | Status | Why this status | Install hint |
30	|---|---|---|---|---|
31	| `spec-kit` (skills mode) | [`github/spec-kit`](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) | `evaluated` | The de facto SDD framework (95.5k ⭐). 30+ supported agents. Has a `--skills` install mode that ships its slash commands as agent skills. Documented in [`reference/sdd-and-harnesses.md`](../../reference/sdd-and-harnesses.md). Not vendored — would compete with the per-skill philosophy of this repo. | `uvx --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit specify init <project> --integration claude-code --integration-options="--skills"` |
32	| `get-shit-done` (gsd) | [`gsd-build/get-shit-done`](https://github.com/gsd-build/get-shit-done) | `evaluated` | Earlier, lighter SDD (61.4k ⭐). 6-command loop (`gsd-new-project → gsd-discuss-phase → gsd-plan-phase → gsd-execute-phase → gsd-verify-work → gsd-ship`). | (see upstream README) |
33	| `gsd-2` | [`gsd-build/gsd-2`](https://github.com/gsd-build/gsd-2) | `evaluated` | Standalone harness (not just a SDD framework). | (see upstream README) |
34	| OpenClaw | [`openclaw/openclaw`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) | `evaluated` | Standalone CLI/runtime that controls the agent session. Also produces `gstack-openclaw-*` skills (already vendored under `product-planning` series). | (see upstream README) |

1	# Domains
2	
3	Per-domain hub pages. Each hub is a single-page entry point that pulls
4	together the local skills, vendored skills, external (manual-install)
5	skills, MCP servers, and backlog items relevant to a professional
6	domain.
7	
8	## Hubs
9	
10	| Hub | Coverage | Status |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| [Finance](finance.md) | Banking, capital markets, equity research, wealth management, fund admin. | Populated |
13	| [Quant Research](quant-research.md) | Quant trading, factor research, backtesting, live execution. | Populated |
14	| [AI/ML Research](ai-ml-research.md) | Experiment tracking, model lifecycle, fine-tuning, agent frameworks. | Populated |
15	| [Web & Fullstack](web-fullstack.md) | Next.js / React / Tailwind / Supabase / Vercel / browser automation / web quality audits. | Populated |
16	| [Knowledge Work](knowledge-work.md) | Sales / legal / customer support / product / marketing / data / etc. | Mostly template |
17	| [Agent Harness](agent-harness.md) | SDD frameworks + agent harnesses (the layer above skills). | Template only |
18	
19	"Mostly template" / "Template only" hubs are honest about being mostly
20	empty — they exist so the structure is in place when content arrives.
21	
22	## How to add a new domain hub
23	
24	1. Copy [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md) to `docs/catalog/domains/<slug>.md`.
25	2. Fill in the elevator pitch + the 4 tables (Local / Vendored / External / MCP) — leave `_none yet_` for empty rows.
26	3. Add the new page to `mkdocs.yml` nav under `Catalog → Domains`.
27	4. Translate to `docs/catalog/domains/<slug>.zh-TW.md` (every catalog page is bilingual).
28	5. Cross-link from related hubs (`See also` section) and from any
29	   relevant reference landscape pages.
30	6. Run `make docs-build` (strict mode catches missing translations and
31	   broken links).
32	
33	For the workflow on adding individual entries to an existing hub
34	(skills, MCPs, status changes), see
35	[Adding catalog entries](../../workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
36
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Warp Oz skills
2	
3	[Warp](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp) (57k⭐) is a terminal that evolved into an
4	"agentic development environment." In May 2026 Warp open-sourced its main
5	codebase under **AGPL-3.0**. Alongside the main repo, the team publishes
6	[`warpdotdev/oz-skills`](https://github.com/warpdotdev/oz-skills) (764⭐)
7	— a growing collection of skills for their **Oz** cloud-agent platform.
8	
9	## Why oz-skills is installable here
10	
11	oz-skills is **MIT-licensed** and follows the
12	[agentskills.io specification](https://agentskills.io/specification), so
13	the skills work in any compliant agent: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor,
14	Gemini CLI. The Warp agent is just another host — the skills themselves are
15	portable markdown.
16	
17	The Warp main repo is AGPL-3.0 (viral copyleft); that license does **not**
18	propagate to oz-skills, which is separately MIT. Vendoring oz-skills into this
19	repo is safe.
20	
21	## Skills we vendor (6 of 15)
22	
23	We pick skills that fill genuine gaps in this repo's existing lineup. Skipped
24	skills: `mcp-builder` (duplicate of `anthropics/mcp-builder`), `webapp-testing`
25	(duplicate of `anthropics/webapp-testing` in the `fullstack-nextjs` series),
26	`scheduler` (too narrow — local-only reminders), `slack-qa-investigate` (Slack
27	dependency), `dbt-model-index` / `analysis-artifacts` (BigQuery-shaped for
28	Warp's internal stack), `terraform-style-check` (too narrow), `seo-aeo-audit`
29	(too opinionated), `docs-update` (overlaps `doc-coauthoring` / the doc-update
30	pattern already in CLAUDE.md).
31	
32	### `github-workflow` plugin — 4 skills
33	
34	| Skill | Description |
35	|---|---|
36	| `ci-fix` | Diagnose GitHub Actions failures: inspect logs via `gh`, identify root cause, implement a minimal fix, push to a dedicated fix branch. Prerequisite: `gh auth status`. |
37	| `create-pull-request` | Create a well-structured PR following project conventions — commit analysis, branch management, PR body via `gh pr create`. |
38	| `github-bug-report-triage` | Evaluate a GitHub bug issue for actionability. Locates the project's bug-report template, checks required fields, and drafts a constructive comment for incomplete reports. |
39	| `github-issue-dedupe` | Detect duplicate issues using multi-strategy semantic + keyword search. Can run manually or be wired into a GitHub Actions workflow. |
40	
41	These complement `engineering-fundamentals/triage` (mattpocock) which is more
42	general-purpose. The Oz skills are GitHub-specific and use the `gh` CLI for
43	automation.
44	
45	### `web-quality` plugin — 2 skills
46	
47	| Skill | Description |
48	|---|---|
49	| `web-accessibility-audit` | WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 compliance audit — identifies violations by POUR principle category, provides remediation steps. Works without an MCP dependency. |
50	| `web-performance-audit` | Core Web Vitals + Lighthouse audit using the `chrome-devtools` MCP. Requires `chrome-devtools-mcp@latest` configured in `.mcp.json`. If not configured, the skill tells you how to add it. |
51	
52	`web-accessibility-audit` is MCP-free and works anywhere. `web-performance-audit`
53	requires the Chrome DevTools MCP — the skill gracefully degrades if it is not
54	present.
55	
56	## Install
57	
58	```bash
59	# All 6 via this repo
60	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills
61	
62	# Or directly from upstream
63	npx skills@latest add warpdotdev/oz-skills/.agents/skills/ci-fix
64	npx skills@latest add warpdotdev/oz-skills/.agents/skills/web-accessibility-audit
65	# ...
66	```
67	
68	## Warp's AGPL-3.0 note
69	
70	The Warp terminal itself is AGPL-3.0. If you embed Warp into a product you
71	ship to users, AGPL requires you to open-source your modifications. Using Warp
72	as a local development tool does not trigger AGPL. Using oz-skills (MIT)
73	separately from Warp has no AGPL implications.
74	
75	## See also
76	
77	- [Browser automation skills](browser-automation-skills.md) — testing web apps
78	  in a real browser; complements the web-quality skills above
79	- [`fullstack-nextjs/webapp-testing`](../skills/webapp-testing.md) — the
80	  Playwright-based Anthropic skill already vendored for frontend QA
81	- [Agent skill compatibility](agent-skill-compatibility.md) — portable
82	  `SKILL.md` spec all these skills follow
83

1	# Catalog
2	
3	A curated index of **external skills, MCP servers, and domain hubs** —
4	distinct from [Skills](../skills/index.md) (what we ship) and
5	[Reference](../reference/scripts.md) (how *our* tooling works).
6	
7	The catalog exists because:
8	
9	- Some skills are worth knowing about but not vendoring (license,
10	  scope, niche, plugin-only) — we still want them findable from the
11	  docs.
12	- MCP servers don't fit cleanly into the skill model — they need a
13	  separate record area.
14	- A domain practitioner (finance, ML, quant, …) wants one entry point
15	  that lists relevant local + vendored + external skills + MCPs +
16	  backlog items together.
17	
18	## What's in here
19	
20	| Subarea | Purpose | Start here |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| [Domains](domains/index.md) | One hub page per professional domain — pulls together skills + MCPs + backlog from the domain's perspective. | [Finance](domains/finance.md) is the most-populated example. |
23	| [External skills](skill-collections.md) | Single curated index of upstream skill collections + adjacent reading. Replaces the historical `Collections.md` + README "Resources" section. | The full table at the top of the page. |
24	| [MCP wiki](mcp/index.md) | Personal-knowledge area for MCP servers — one page per MCP with frontmatter for future automation. | [Financial Datasets MCP](mcp/financialdatasets-ai.md) is the first populated entry. |
25	
26	## How catalog status works
27	
28	Every external entry carries a `status:` value (`vendored / deferred /
29	skipped / evaluated / wishlist`) that doubles as a vendoring decision
30	log. The full enum lives in
31	[`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/docs/_snippets/external-install.md)
32	and is included at the top of every catalog page that lists external
33	entries.
34	
35	Workflow for status changes — see
36	[Adding catalog entries](../workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
37	
38	## See also (Reference landscapes)
39	
40	The [Reference](../reference/scripts.md) section already contains

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills`. Contains custom-authored skills (`skills/local/`) and cherry-picked 3rd-party skills (`skills/vendor/`) synced from upstream repos.
8	
9	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	```bash
14	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
15	make sync
16	
17	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
18	make sync-check
19	
20	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
21	make kanban
22	
23	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
24	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
25	make marketplace
26	
27	# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
28	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
29	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
30	# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
31	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
32	
33	# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)
34	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
35	  --title "Title" --description "Description"
36	
37	# Triage backlog/inbox.md (loose captures) into TODO.md
38	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh             # interactive
39	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines
40	
41	# Move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
42	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
43	
44	# Create a new local skill
45	cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
46	
47	# Docs site (MkDocs Material + llmstxt + copy-to-llm)
48	uv sync --extra docs
49	make docs-serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
50	make docs-build     # produces ./site/
51	```
52	
53	## Vendor System
54	
55	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
56	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
57	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
58	
59	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA.
60	
61	Active series in this repo:
62	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
63	
64	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
65	
66	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
67	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
68	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
69	
70	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
71	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
72	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
73	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
74	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
75	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
76	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
77	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
78	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
79	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
80	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
81	
82	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
83	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
84	
85	## Marketplace Catalog
86	
87	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
88	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
89	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
90	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
91	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
92	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
93	for the full mechanism.
94	
95	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
96	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
97	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
98	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
99	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
100	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
101	
102	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
103	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
104	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
105	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
106	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
107	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
108	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
109	within-group caveat in
110	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
111	
112	## SKILL.md Format
113	
114	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
115	
116	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
117	
118	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
119	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
120	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
121	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
122	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
123	
124	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
125	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
126	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
127	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
128	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
129	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
130	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
131	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
132	
133	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
134	
135	```bash
136	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
137	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
138	
139	# …or remove them afterward
140	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
141	```
142	
143	## Project Memory Workflow
144	
145	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
146	
147	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
148	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
149	
150	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
151	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
152	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
153	
154	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
155	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
156	
157	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
158	
159	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
160	
161	   ```bash
162	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
163	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
164	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
165	   ```
166	
167	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
168	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
169	
170	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
171	
172	   ```bash
173	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
174	   ```
175	
176	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
177	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
178	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
179	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
180	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
181	
182	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
183	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
184	   afterwards to catch drift.
185	
186	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
187	
188	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
189	
190	```bash
191	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
192	```
193	
194	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
195	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
196	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
197	
198	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
199	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
200	
201	### External skill / MCP / domain catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
202	
203	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
204	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
205	own conventions). It has three subareas:
206	
207	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
208	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
209	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
210	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
211	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
212	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
213	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
214	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
215	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
216	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
217	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
218	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
219	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
220	  status / license / last_verified`).
221	
222	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
223	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
224	
225	| Status | Meaning |
226	|---|---|
227	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
228	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
229	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
230	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
231	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
232	
233	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
234	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
235	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
236	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
237	
238	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
239	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
240	
241	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
242	
243	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
244	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
245	
246	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
247	2. The root cause
248	3. The workaround
249	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
250	
251	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
252	the explanation they do not know yet.
253

1	# Deep Research landscape
2	
3	This page surveys the **commercial Deep Research products** from major AI
4	vendors and the **open-source skills/frameworks** that try to reproduce
5	similar capability locally. It also explains what this repo vendors
6	(`deep-research/`) and which adjacent options are deliberately *not*
7	vendored.
8	
9	## Commercial Deep Research products (2024–2026)
10	
11	The five major vendors converged on a similar shape — multi-agent
12	planning, parallel retrieval, citation-grounded synthesis — but with
13	different defaults around browser scope, model size, and pricing.
14	
15	| Vendor | Product | Launched | Architecture | Notable |
16	|---|---|---|---|---|
17	| **OpenAI** | ChatGPT Deep Research (`o3-deep-research`, `o4-mini-deep-research`) | 2025-02 | Plan → multi-step search → cited report | Plus 25/mo, Pro 250/mo; 2026-02 added scoped sites + collaborative planning + live progress |
18	| **Google** | Gemini Deep Research (Interactions API) | 2024-12 | Lead agent + parallel sub-agents + synthesis agent | Hooks into Gmail/Drive/Chat; 1M-token context; Canvas visualizations; 2026-04 added MCP tool connectors |
19	| **xAI** | Grok DeepSearch / DeeperSearch / Grok 4 Heavy | 2024-Q2 → 2025-07 | Multi-agent parallel reasoning, live X + web search | 256k token context; no formal citations yet; emphasizes raw performance |
20	| **Anthropic** | Claude Research | 2025-06 (eng blog) | LeadResearcher + sub-agents + CitationAgent | ~90% accuracy uplift over single-agent (Opus 4 lead + Sonnet 4 sub); strict enterprise privacy |
21	| **Meta** | (no first-party DR product) | — | — | LLaMA 4 Scout/Maverick are multimodal foundation models; deep-research must be assembled from LangChain / LlamaIndex / vector DBs |
22	
23	The shared pattern across all four shipping products:
24	
25	1. **Plan** — decompose query into sub-questions
26	2. **Parallel retrieve** — spawn sub-agents that hit web search / docs / files
27	3. **Iterate** — re-plan based on what's found, follow citations
28	4. **Synthesize** — assemble a cited report (markdown / HTML / PDF)
29	
30	Typical wall time is 2–20 minutes; cost is gated by subscription tier or
31	per-call API metering.
32	
33	## Reproducing Deep Research locally — the six layers
34	
35	A real "deep research" stack for an agent CLI is **not a single skill**.
36	Decompose it into six layers; pick a tool per layer:
37	
38	| Layer | What it does | Representative tools |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| 1. **Planning / decomposition** | Turn the question into sub-questions, evidence requirements, and a research plan | `199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill` (vendored), `langchain-ai/deepagents` (Python framework, *not* a skill) |
41	| 2. **Retrieval** | Web / news / GitHub / PDF search | [`tavily-ai/skills/tavily-search`](https://github.com/tavily-ai/skills), [`firecrawl/cli/skills/firecrawl-search`](https://github.com/firecrawl/cli) |
42	| 3. **Extraction** | Pull main content, tables, multi-page text out of fetched URLs | `firecrawl-scrape`, `firecrawl-crawl`, `firecrawl-parse` |
43	| 4. **Browser interaction** | Login walls, JS rendering, dynamic UIs, downloads | [`vercel-labs/agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) (32k⭐), [`browser-use/browser-use`](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) (93k⭐) |
44	| 5. **Evidence management** | Source registry, claim ledger, citation verification | `199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill` (built-in) |
45	| 6. **Synthesis** | Final report (markdown / HTML / PDF) with inline citations | `199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill`, `tavily-ai/skills/tavily-research` |
46	
47	The 2-skill minimum that gets you something usable: **(1) + (5) + (6)**
48	from one disciplined research-flow skill, plus **(2)** from a search
49	backend you trust.
50	
51	## What this repo vendors
52	
53	Just **one** skill, deliberately:
54	
55	- **`vendor/deep-research/deep-research`** — from
56	  [`199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill`](https://github.com/199-biotechnologies/claude-deep-research-skill)

## 4. SKILL.md frontmatter catalog (name + description)

1. **grill-with-docs** — A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
2. **tdd** — Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
3. **diagnosing-bugs** — Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
4. **zoom-out** — Tell the agent to zoom out and give broader context or a higher-level perspective. Use when you're unfamiliar with a section of code or need to understand how it fits into the bigger picture. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`; frozen skill)*
5. **to-prd** — Turn the current conversation into a PRD and publish it to the project issue tracker — no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
6. **to-issues** — Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable issues on the project issue tracker using tracer-bullet vertical slices. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
7. **improve-codebase-architecture** — Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
8. **triage** — Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles — categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs. *(also `disable-model-invocation: true`)*
9. **prototype** — Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

# Docs structure & conventions report — for adding a Matt Pocock collection page

## 1. Overall `docs/` tree structure

The site is MkDocs Material with a bilingual (`i18n` suffix) setup. Every published page has a `*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md` pair. Top-level organization:

```
docs/
  index.md                     Home
  getting-started.md
  conventions.md
  changelog.md
  _snippets/                   EN-only include fragments (NOT rendered as pages)
    install.md
    external-install.md        <- status-enum single source of truth
    domain-hub-template.md     <- the domain hub _template (EN-only)
  workflows/                   How-to guides
    adding-vendor-skills.md
    adding-catalog-entries.md  <- catalog recipe
    creating-local-skills.md
    project-memory.md
  skills/                      One page per shipped skill (local + vendored) + index.md
    index.md, <skill>.md ...
  catalog/                     Vendoring decision log + external awareness
    index.md
    skill-collections.md       <- the upstream-collections index
    domains/                   Per-domain hub pages + index.md
      index.md, finance.md, quant-research.md, ai-ml-research.md,
      web-fullstack.md, knowledge-work.md, agent-harness.md
    mcp/                        MCP wiki (index.md + one page per MCP)
      index.md, financialdatasets-ai.md
  reference/                   Landscape / convention pages (things we consume, not ship)
    warp-oz-skills.md, deep-research-landscape.md, sdd-and-harnesses.md,
    llm-wiki-pattern.md, npx-skills-metadata.md, tag-schema.md, ... (16 pages)

## 3. `docs/catalog/domains/` hubs + the template

**Hub pages present:** `finance.md`, `quant-research.md`, `ai-ml-research.md`, `web-fullstack.md`, `knowledge-work.md`, `agent-harness.md` (each + `.zh-TW.md`), plus `index.md`.

**Template** (`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`, EN-only) structure:
- `# {{Domain name}}` + one-line elevator pitch.
- `## Skills in this repo` → `### Local` (table `Skill | One-line | Notes`) and `### Vendored` (table `Skill | Upstream | Series`).
- `## External skills (manual install)` → `--8<-- "_snippets/external-install.md"` include, then table `Skill / Plugin | Upstream | Status | Why this status | Install hint`.
- `## MCP servers` → table `Name | Upstream | Status | Auth | Records`.
- `## Backlog (TODO P?)` → bullet list linking `TODO.md` anchors.
- `## See also` → reference-landscape + adjacent-hub links.
- Header comment instructs: copy to `docs/catalog/domains/<slug>.md`, add to `mkdocs.yml` nav under `Catalog → Domains`, and keep `_none yet_` placeholders rather than padding.

**How skills are referenced in a hub:** by backticked skill name, linked either to its `docs/skills/<name>.md` page (for shipped skills) or to the upstream repo (for external ones). The Vendored table cites the `Series` column (e.g. `engineering-fundamentals`, `fullstack-nextjs`).

Its `## See also` already name-drops mattpocock: the Warp Oz reference page (line 41) says *"These complement `engineering-fundamentals/triage` (mattpocock) which is more general-purpose."* mattpocock's skills (TDD, diagnosing bugs, triage, prototype, PRD/issues authoring, architecture improvement, doc-grilling) are coding-workflow/engineering-fundamentals oriented — **there is currently no "engineering" or "coding-workflow" domain hub**. So there's no perfectly-matching populated hub; the engineering-fundamentals series is vendored but under-represented in the domains layer.

## 5. `mkdocs.yml` nav wiring

Path: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/mkdocs.yml`. Key mechanics:
- `plugins.i18n` with `docs_structure: suffix`, `fallback_to_default: true`, locales `en` (default) + `zh-TW`. Only the EN `*.md` paths appear in `nav:`; zh-TW is auto-derived from the suffix.
- `plugins.llmstxt.sections.Catalog` globs `catalog/*.md`, `catalog/domains/*.md`, `catalog/mcp/*.md` — a new `catalog/*.md` page is auto-picked-up by the llms.txt output.
- `pymdownx.snippets.base_path` includes `.`, `docs`, `docs/_snippets` (that's why `--8<-- "_snippets/external-install.md"` resolves).

**The `Catalog` nav block (lines 142-155):**

```yaml
  - Catalog:
      - Overview: catalog/index.md
      - Domains:
          - Overview: catalog/domains/index.md
          - Finance: catalog/domains/finance.md
          - Quant Research: catalog/domains/quant-research.md
          - AI/ML Research: catalog/domains/ai-ml-research.md
          - Web & Fullstack: catalog/domains/web-fullstack.md
          - Knowledge Work: catalog/domains/knowledge-work.md
          - Agent Harness: catalog/domains/agent-harness.md
      - External skills: catalog/skill-collections.md
      - MCP wiki:
          - Overview: catalog/mcp/index.md
          - Financial Datasets: catalog/mcp/financialdatasets-ai.md
```

**Where a new collection/series page would register:** there is **no existing "Collections" nav group** — `skill-collections.md` sits as a single leaf `External skills:` under `Catalog`. Grouping patterns that already exist you could mirror:
- Under `Catalog`: the `Domains:` and `MCP wiki:` sub-groups each use an `Overview:` index page + sibling leaves. A new "Collections" or "Series deep-dives" sub-group would follow that shape.
- Under `Skills` → `Vendored` (lines 127-141): the `Fullstack Next.js:` **series** is a nested nav group listing each skill page. This is the established "series grouping" precedent in nav — but note it lists individual skill pages, not a single series-intro page.
- Under `Reference` (lines 156-171): flat leaves, where the single-author deep-dives (`Warp Oz skills`, `Deep Research landscape`) currently live.

`not_in_nav: /_snippets/` suppresses the snippet/template from nav. `validation.links.not_found: info` keeps `--strict` builds passing.

**Gap worth flagging:** the `engineering-fundamentals` (mattpocock) and `product-planning` series are vendored in `vendor.yaml` / `skills/vendor/` but have **no** individual `docs/skills/*.md` pages and **no** nav entries — only `fullstack-nextjs` is documented under `Skills → Vendored`. So a mattpocock page would be net-new documentation surface, and there's a decision to make about whether to also add the 9 individual skill pages the way `fullstack-nextjs` did.

## 6. Status-enum source of truth + catalog recipe

**`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`** is the status-enum single source of truth. It's an admonition block: *"Status enum (single source of truth across the catalog)"* with a 5-row table:

| Status | Meaning | Where it links |
|---|---|---|
| `vendored` | Already in `vendor.yaml`. | Link to `skills/vendor/<name>/` (or series). |
| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` — under consideration. | Link to the `TODO.md` anchor. |
| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor. | Inline reason required (1 sentence). |
| `evaluated` | Read but no decision. Effectively "tracked." | Inline 1-line note. |
| `wishlist` | Surfaced, not yet evaluated. | No link required; default for fresh discoveries. |

It also carries the "Manual install for non-vendored skills" tip (the `npx skills@latest add <owner>/<repo>[/<path>] [-s <name>] [--full-depth]` commands, and the `claude plugin marketplace add` / `claude plugin install` path for plugin marketplaces). This snippet is `--8<--` included at the top of `skill-collections.md`, every domain hub, and the `adding-catalog-entries.md` workflow — so all pages show one canonical enum.

**`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`** recipe summary:
- "When to write a catalog entry" table maps discovery → destination page → starting status (external skill → `skill-collections.md` + a domain hub, start `wishlist`; new MCP → new `catalog/mcp/<slug>.md`; new domain → copy `_template.md`; rejected → `skipped`; looked-but-undecided → `evaluated`).
- Includes the enum via the same snippet.
- **Status-change recipes** (each is: run a script, then edit the catalog row):
  - `wishlist → deferred`: `./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P? --effort <S|M|L> --title ... --description ...`, then change `status: wishlist`→`deferred` and link the TODO line.
  - `deferred → vendored`: `./scripts/add-vendor.sh <owner>/<repo>/<path>` (or `--series <series-name> ...`), optionally `./scripts/promote-todo.sh`, then change status→`vendored` and repoint link to `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`.
  - `→ skipped`: just edit status + add a one-sentence inline reason.
- "Adding a new MCP entry" (6 steps: create file w/ YAML frontmatter, fill 6-section body, translate to zh-TW, add to nav, add index row, cross-link hub).
- "Adding a new domain hub" defers to `domains/index.md#how-to-add-a-new-domain-hub`.
- **Bilingual obligation** restated: every `docs/catalog/` page except snippet/`_template.md` needs a `*.zh-TW.md` twin in the same PR.
- **Validation:** `make docs-build` (strict — catches missing snippets/broken links), `make marketplace`, `make kanban`; then `make docs-serve` and click cross-links.

The `add-vendor.sh --series` flow and the rename/freeze bookkeeping are documented further in `CLAUDE.md` (Vendor System) and `docs/workflows/adding-vendor-skills.md#series-grouping`.

## 7. Precedent: single-upstream-author "series introduction / collection deep-dive"

**Closest precedent — `docs/reference/warp-oz-skills.md`** (a single-author collection deep-dive). This is the strongest model to follow. Its structure:
- `#` title + intro paragraph (what the upstream is, stars, license, what they publish).
- `## Why <collection> is installable here` — licensing/portability rationale.
- `## Skills we vendor (6 of 15)` — states the cherry-pick count, then a paragraph enumerating **skipped** skills with one-line reasons each (mirrors the vendoring-policy "we do not vendor when" logic).
- Per-plugin subsections (`### <plugin> — N skills`) each with a `Skill | Description` table.
- `## Install` — `npx skills@latest add` whole-repo and per-skill upstream commands.
- License/legal note section.
- `## See also` — cross-links to related reference pages and vendored skill docs.

It lives in **Reference**, not Catalog (per `catalog/index.md`: reference-landscape pages document conventions/rationale rather than track external entries; the catalog cross-links them). It is registered in nav under `Reference` (`mkdocs.yml` line 171: `Warp Oz skills: reference/warp-oz-skills.md`) and is referenced from the `skill-collections.md` mattpocock-adjacent Warp row.

**Second precedent — `docs/reference/deep-research-landscape.md`** (a single-skill-series deep-dive for `199-biotechnologies/deep-research`). Broader "landscape survey" shape (commercial-products table, layer decomposition, "what this repo vendors," "adjacent options not vendored — and why" table). Good model if you want the mattpocock page to also survey the space rather than just enumerate the 9 skills.

**Series-in-nav precedent — `Skills → Vendored → Fullstack Next.js`** (`docs/skills/index.md` §"Fullstack Next.js series", lines 58-74, and `mkdocs.yml` lines 132-141): a `series:` intro paragraph + a `Skill | Upstream | Detailed page` table, with each skill getting its own `docs/skills/<name>.md`. This is the precedent if you want the mattpocock page to live under `Skills` as a series index with per-skill pages, rather than as a Reference deep-dive.

**Recommendation implied by the conventions (for your planning):** the repo already treats mattpocock as a `vendored (partial)` collection with a `series: engineering-fundamentals`. The two clean options that match existing precedent are (a) a `docs/reference/mattpocock-engineering-fundamentals.md` deep-dive modeled on `warp-oz-skills.md`, linked from the mattpocock row in `skill-collections.md` (exactly as Warp Oz and deep-research do) and registered under `Reference` in nav; or (b) a `Skills → Vendored → Engineering Fundamentals` series section modeled on `Fullstack Next.js`, with 9 per-skill pages. Either way you'll owe a `.zh-TW.md` twin for any `catalog/` page (a Reference page also conventionally gets one — all `reference/*.md` are paired), a nav entry, and — worth fixing in the same PR — the stale `diagnose`/`zoom-out` names in the `skill-collections.md` mattpocock row (now `diagnosing-bugs` + frozen `zoom-out`).

1	# Warp Oz skills
2	
3	[Warp](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp) (57k⭐) is a terminal that evolved into an
4	"agentic development environment." In May 2026 Warp open-sourced its main
5	codebase under **AGPL-3.0**. Alongside the main repo, the team publishes
6	[`warpdotdev/oz-skills`](https://github.com/warpdotdev/oz-skills) (764⭐)
7	— a growing collection of skills for their **Oz** cloud-agent platform.
8	
9	## Why oz-skills is installable here
10	
11	oz-skills is **MIT-licensed** and follows the
12	[agentskills.io specification](https://agentskills.io/specification), so
13	the skills work in any compliant agent: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor,
14	Gemini CLI. The Warp agent is just another host — the skills themselves are
15	portable markdown.
16	
17	The Warp main repo is AGPL-3.0 (viral copyleft); that license does **not**
18	propagate to oz-skills, which is separately MIT. Vendoring oz-skills into this
19	repo is safe.
20	
21	## Skills we vendor (6 of 15)
22	
23	We pick skills that fill genuine gaps in this repo's existing lineup. Skipped
24	skills: `mcp-builder` (duplicate of `anthropics/mcp-builder`), `webapp-testing`

29	(too opinionated), `docs-update` (overlaps `doc-coauthoring` / the doc-update
30	pattern already in CLAUDE.md).

32	### `github-workflow` plugin — 4 skills
33	
34	| Skill | Description |
35	|---|---|
36	| `ci-fix` | Diagnose GitHub Actions failures: inspect logs via `gh`, identify root cause, implement a minimal fix, push to a dedicated fix branch. Prerequisite: `gh auth status`. |
37	| `create-pull-request` | Create a well-structured PR following project conventions — commit analysis, branch management, PR body via `gh pr create`. |
38	| `github-bug-report-triage` | Evaluate a GitHub bug issue for actionability. Locates the project's bug-report template, checks required fields, and drafts a constructive comment for incomplete reports. |
39	| `github-issue-dedupe` | Detect duplicate issues using multi-strategy semantic + keyword search. Can run manually or be wired into a GitHub Actions workflow. |
40	
41	These complement `engineering-fundamentals/triage` (mattpocock) which is more

43	automation.

77	## Vendoring policy
78	
79	We vendor a skill when:
80	
81	1. The upstream has stable canonical authority (Vercel for Next.js, Supabase for Supabase, etc.).
82	2. The skill fills a gap not already covered by another vendored or local skill.
83	3. The license is compatible with the [agentskills.io specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).
84	
85	We **do not** vendor when:
86	
87	- The upstream is itself a marketplace / collection (we cherry-pick instead).
88	- Plugin-format collections (e.g., `anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins`) require `claude plugin install` rather than `npx skills add` — we record them here for manual install.
89	- The skill duplicates an already-vendored one from a more authoritative source.
90	- The skill is too narrow for general use (host-specific, BigQuery-specific, etc.).
91	
92	For the full workflow — including how to move an entry from `wishlist` →
93	`deferred` → `vendored` — see
94	[Adding catalog entries](../workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).

Summary — end-to-end workflow and how skills chain together

Workflow (high level)
1. Align language and detect collisions (grilling + CONTEXT.md)
2. Turn conversation into durable plan/spec (to-prd → to-issues → triage)
3. Prepare agent-ready tasks (triage produces AGENT-BRIEF → ready-for-agent)
4. Implement with tight feedback loops (tdd tracer-bullet + diagnose)
5. Improve design and prevent long-term rot (improve-codebase-architecture + zoom-out)
6. Protect operations and ergonomics (misc guardrails, pre-commit, caveman for terse comms)
This is an iteration: grill → spec/tickets → narrow slice implementation → automated observable tests → refactor/architecture review → repeat.

Skills named (as they appear in the article)
- diagnose
- grill-with-docs
- triage
- improve-codebase-architecture
- setup-matt-pocock-skills
- tdd
- to-issues
- to-prd
- zoom-out
- caveman
- grill-me
- write-a-skill
- git-guardrails-claude-code
- migrate-to-shoehorn
- scaffold-exercises
- setup-pre-commit
- CONTEXT.md (document / shared-language artifact)
- AGENT-BRIEF.md (artifact)
- OUT-OF-SCOPE (.out-of-scope/ files)
- scripts/link-skills.sh
- scripts/list-skills.sh
- personal/ (bucket)
- deprecated/ (bucket)

Mapping skills to failure modes / responsibilities
- Avoiding wrong agent behavior: grill-me, grill-with-docs (domain collision detection; update CONTEXT.md)
- Reducing verbose/unfocused output: CONTEXT.md, shared language, caveman
- Making code actually work: tdd (tracer-bullet style) and diagnose (observability bootstrap)
- Preventing architectural decay: to-prd, zoom-out, improve-codebase-architecture
- Operational safety and repeatable setup: git-guardrails-claude-code, setup-pre-commit, setup-matt-pocock-skills

Key philosophy points (quoted short phrases from article where useful)
- Skills are small, composable primitives that are meant for “real engineering” (quote: "real engineering" — contextualized)
- Design favors splitting failure modes and applying a focused skill to each (quote: "They work with any model." — used as a slogan about process portability)
- Emphasize tracer-bullet tests over horizontal slicing: one behavior → one test → minimal code
- Build machine-observable feedback loops before deep code inspection (diagnose: create a reproducible loop so the agent can observe pass/fail)
- Treat issue/tracking artifacts as durable contracts for agents (AGENT-BRIEF as authoritative spec; keep out-of-scope records)

Practical adoption guidance (concise)

## Process

2. Sketch out the seams at which you're going to test the feature. Existing seams should be preferred to new ones. Use the highest seam possible. If new seams are needed, propose them at the highest point you can. The fewer seams across the codebase, the better - the ideal number is one.

The problem that the user is facing, from the user's perspective.

## Solution

The solution to the problem, from the user's perspective.

## User Stories

A LONG, numbered list of user stories. Each user story should be in the format of:

===== engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md =====
---
name: to-tickets
description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker — edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# To Tickets

Break a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets** — tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

### 1. Gather context

Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.

<vertical-slice-rules>

- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) — vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window
- Any prefactoring should be done first

</vertical-slice-rules>

Give each ticket its **blocking edges** — the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.

**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol — whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket — green is promised only there.

===== engineering/implement/SKILL.md =====
---
name: implement
description: "Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets."
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Implement the work described by the user in the spec or tickets.

Use /tdd where possible, at pre-agreed seams.

Run typechecking regularly, single test files regularly, and the full test suite once at the end.

Once done, use /code-review to review the work.

Commit your work to the current branch.

14	usage() {
15	  cat <<EOF
16	Usage: $(basename "$0") [OPTIONS] <owner/repo[/path/to/skill]>
17	
18	Add a vendored skill to vendor.yaml and optionally sync it.
19	
20	Examples:
21	  $(basename "$0") marimo-team/skills/skills/marimo-notebook
22	  $(basename "$0") vercel-labs/agent-skills/skills/next-js
23	  $(basename "$0") --name my-skill --branch dev owner/repo/skills/my-skill
24	  $(basename "$0") --no-sync owner/repo/skills/some-skill
25	  $(basename "$0") --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
26	
27	Options:
28	  --name NAME      Override the skill name (default: last path component)
29	  --series SERIES  Group under skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/ (default: flat)
30	  --branch BRANCH  Upstream branch (default: main)
31	  --no-sync        Only add to vendor.yaml, don't sync immediately
32	  -h, --help       Show this help message
33	
34	Dependencies: gh (GitHub CLI), yq (YAML processor)
35	EOF
36	}
37	
38	check_deps() {
39	  local missing=()
40	  command -v gh &>/dev/null || missing+=(gh)
41	  command -v yq &>/dev/null || missing+=(yq)
42	  if [[ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
43	    echo -e "${RED}Error: Missing dependencies: ${missing[*]}${NC}" >&2
44	    if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
45	      echo "  macOS:  brew install ${missing[*]}" >&2
46	    else
47	      echo "  Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install ${missing[*]}" >&2
48	      echo "  Fedora/RHEL:   sudo dnf install ${missing[*]}" >&2
49	      echo "  Arch:          sudo pacman -S ${missing[*]}" >&2
50	      echo "  Or via: snap install ${missing[*]}" >&2
51	    fi
52	    exit 1
53	  fi
54	  if ! gh auth status &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
55	    echo -e "${RED}Error: gh is not authenticated. Run 'gh auth login' first.${NC}" >&2
56	    exit 1
57	  fi
58	}
59	
60	# Parse owner/repo/path from a single argument
61	# Accepts formats:
62	#   owner/repo/path/to/skill
63	#   https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
64	parse_source() {
65	  local input="$1"
66	
67	  # Strip GitHub URL prefix if present
68	  input="${input#https://github.com/}"
69	  input="${input#http://github.com/}"
70	
71	  # Strip /tree/<branch>/ from URL-style paths
72	  if [[ "$input" =~ ^([^/]+/[^/]+)/tree/([^/]+)/(.+)$ ]]; then
73	    local url_branch="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
74	    input="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}/${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
75	    # Use URL branch as default if --branch not explicitly set
76	    if [[ -z "$OPT_BRANCH_SET" ]]; then
77	      OPT_BRANCH="$url_branch"
78	    fi
79	  fi
80	
81	  # Remove trailing slash
82	  input="${input%/}"
83	
84	  # Need at least owner/repo; path may be "." for repo-root SKILL.md
85	  local slash_count
86	  slash_count=$(echo "$input" | tr -cd '/' | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
87	  if [[ "$slash_count" -lt 1 ]]; then
88	    echo -e "${RED}Error: Expected format: owner/repo[/path/to/skill]${NC}" >&2
89	    echo "  Got: $input" >&2
90	    exit 1
91	  fi
92	
93	  # Extract owner and repo (first two components); rest is path (may be empty)
94	  PARSED_OWNER="$(echo "$input" | cut -d'/' -f1)"
95	  PARSED_REPO="$(echo "$input" | cut -d'/' -f2)"
96	  if [[ "$slash_count" -lt 2 ]]; then
97	    PARSED_PATH="."
98	  else
99	    PARSED_PATH="$(echo "$input" | cut -d'/' -f3-)"
100	  fi
101	}
102	
103	main() {
104	  local opt_name=""
105	  local opt_series=""
106	  OPT_BRANCH="main"
107	  OPT_BRANCH_SET=""
108	  local opt_sync=true
109	  local positional=""
110	
111	  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
112	    case "$1" in
113	      --name) opt_name="$2"; shift 2 ;;
114	      --series) opt_series="$2"; shift 2 ;;
115	      --branch) OPT_BRANCH="$2"; OPT_BRANCH_SET=1; shift 2 ;;
116	      --no-sync) opt_sync=false; shift ;;
117	      -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
118	      -*) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;
119	      *) positional="$1"; shift ;;
120	    esac
121	  done
122	
123	  if [[ -z "$positional" ]]; then
124	    echo -e "${RED}Error: Missing required argument${NC}" >&2
125	    usage
126	    exit 1
127	  fi
128	
129	  check_deps
130	
131	  parse_source "$positional"
132	
133	  # Default skill name: basename of path, or repo name when path is "."
134	  local default_name
135	  if [[ "$PARSED_PATH" == "." ]]; then
136	    default_name="$PARSED_REPO"
137	  else
138	    default_name="$(basename "$PARSED_PATH")"
139	  fi
140	  local name="${opt_name:-$default_name}"
141	  local owner="$PARSED_OWNER"
142	  local repo="$PARSED_REPO"
143	  local path="$PARSED_PATH"
144	  local branch="$OPT_BRANCH"
145	
146	  # Verify the upstream path exists
147	  echo -n "Verifying upstream $owner/$repo/$path@$branch... "
148	  local verify_path="$path"
149	  [[ "$verify_path" == "." ]] && verify_path=""
150	  if ! gh api "repos/$owner/$repo/contents/$verify_path?ref=$branch" &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
151	    echo -e "${RED}not found${NC}"
152	    echo -e "${RED}Error: Path '$path' not found in $owner/$repo (branch: $branch)${NC}" >&2
153	    exit 1
154	  fi
155	  echo -e "${GREEN}found${NC}"
156	
157	  # Check for duplicates
158	  if [[ -f "$VENDOR_YAML" ]]; then
159	    local existing
160	    existing=$(yq ".skills[] | select(.name == \"$name\") | .name" "$VENDOR_YAML" 2>/dev/null || true)
161	    if [[ -n "$existing" ]]; then
162	      echo -e "${YELLOW}Skill '$name' already exists in vendor.yaml${NC}"
163	      echo "Use --name to specify a different name, or edit vendor.yaml manually."
164	      exit 1
165	    fi
166	  fi
167	
168	  # Append to vendor.yaml
169	  echo -n "Adding '$name' to vendor.yaml... "
170	  yq -i ".skills += [{

172	    \"upstream\": {

175	      \"path\": \"$path\",
